title: Prepare Nodics for Deployment
readerIntent: Turn a validated project composition into a repeatable deployment candidate without changing module contracts.
priorKnowledge: Understand configuration, topology, providers, security, data exchange, and testing.
owner: Customer project deployment modules and operators using reusable Nodics runtime contracts
summary: Deployment packages the chosen module-based topology, supplies governed configuration and secrets, validates providers and data changes, and proves rollout, health, drain, rollback, and recovery before traffic.

sections.heading: Define the candidate
items: Pin the Nodics, project, generated artifacts, documentation pack, runtime, and provider versions.
Declare environment, server, and optional node packages through package.json.nodics metadata and parent relationships.
Select local activeModules for each runnable process and define remote endpoints under servers.*; do not equate a fixed server list with module ownership.
Document topology, ports, trust boundaries, dependencies, service objectives, capacity assumptions, persistent state, queues, scheduled ownership, and failure behavior.

sections.heading: Supply governed configuration
items: Keep defaults and overrideable behavior in layered config/properties.js; package.json contains only module/runtime metadata.
Provide secrets through approved external or secret-manager layers, never committed files, images, generated context, import data, or logs.
Configure tenant/enterprise policy, route exposure, exact origins, TLS/proxy behavior, strict authentication state, database, cache, search, events, AI, storage, and other providers.
Preview, approve, activate, audit, and roll back only runtime-mutable contracts owned by the existing governance services; static startup configuration remains authoritative.

sections.heading: Prepare state and compatibility
items: Back up authoritative data and verify restoration before schema, identity, index, publication, or provider migration.
Use Nodics import/export and migration contracts; never introduce a deployment-only database write path.
Run idempotent bootstrap/import/migration against an isolated environment, repeat it to prove safe convergence, and retain redacted audit evidence.
Check backward/forward compatibility across APIs, schemas, events, indexes, caches, jobs, workflows, clients, and rolling process versions.

sections.heading: Qualify and release
items: Run focused, governance, positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, resilience, security, performance, topology, upgrade, recovery, and regression suites.
Qualify real production-like providers and distributed behavior; local placeholders and MonoServer results are not production evidence.
Verify liveness, readiness, protected diagnostics, safe telemetry, graceful drain, bounded shutdown, resource cleanup, restart/reconciliation, and rollback.
Use a staged rollout with explicit go/no-go criteria, monitoring, owners, rollback trigger, credential-rotation plan, and post-release verification.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How To Prepare For Deployment
paragraphs: Deployment means preparing Nodics to run safely in a target environment.
Deployment is not only copying files to a server. It includes configuration, generated artifacts, tests, data, security, and operational checks.

sections.heading: Beginner Summary
paragraphs: Deployment is the point where a Nodics runtime must be predictable.
Before deploying, a team should know:

```text
Do not deploy behavior that cannot be rebuilt, tested, explained, and rolled back.
```
items: which project is being deployed;
which environment is targeted;
which servers and nodes will run;
which modules are active in each process;
which tenants are allowed;
which database, cache, search, messaging, import/export, and storage providers are configured;
which APIs are exposed;
which tests prove the release.

sections.heading: Clean-Checkout Release Gate
paragraphs: Use the governed release gate to prove the repository can be installed, cleaned, built, regenerated, documented, and tested from a clean checkout.
Print the gate without running it:
Execute the release-candidate gate with full validation:
The standard gate runs `npm ci`, `npm run clean`, `npm run build`, `npm run llm:validate`, `npm run quality:docs`, and `npm run test:basic`. The full gate also runs `npm run test:full`.

sections.heading: Run Tests
paragraphs: Run live release tests only against isolated approved infrastructure.

sections.heading: Verify Topology
paragraphs: Consolidated mode means one server runs many capabilities together.
Modular mode means capabilities run in separate server processes.

Nodics supports both styles because different deployments need different runtime boundaries. Local development may prefer one process. Enterprise deployments may split identity, CMS, workflow, events, scheduled jobs, import/export, and data processing into separate processes.
items: which server owns each active module;
which modules run locally in each process;
which modules are reached through remote server coordinates;
which nodes are allowed to run scheduled jobs;
which providers are active for database, cache, search, and messaging;
where generated reports and diagnostics are written.

sections.heading: Verify Health And Readiness
paragraphs: Use liveness to confirm the process can answer HTTP:
Use readiness to decide whether the process should receive traffic:
Liveness is intentionally low-disclosure and does not require authentication. Readiness is secured with `system.health.readiness.view` and gated by `apiExposure.categories.operationalHealth`.

For production, each server/node process should have its own readiness contract. Provider-specific projects may extend readiness through later modules to check database, cache, search, messaging, storage, import/export locations, required secrets, and scheduled-job ownership.
Read the [Production Operating Model](/docs/operations/production) before using these endpoints as deployment gates.

sections.heading: Verify Data
paragraphs: Also confirm that versioned or publishable business data has a rollback path when the business process requires it. Published content, catalog data, workflow definitions, runtime configuration, and import runs do not depend on manual database repair as the normal recovery strategy.
items: Initial data is idempotent.
Sample data is not required in production.
Tenant data is correctly isolated.
Imports target the correct tenant.
Runtime configuration can be audited and rolled back.

sections.heading: Verify Security
items: Login routes are intentionally pre-authentication.
Internal module routes remain secured.
Permissions are assigned to the right groups.
Service accounts have least privilege.
Secrets are not stored in source-controlled files.
Audit logs do not expose credentials.

sections.heading: Verify Documentation
paragraphs: Documentation should match the deployed behavior.

```bash
npm run docs:coverage:source -- --limit=20
npm run docs:coverage:contracts -- --limit=20
```
Also regenerate and inspect API documentation when routes or schemas changed:
For developer/support environments with contract exposure enabled, verify:
Keep Swagger/OpenAPI secured in shared and production-like topologies.

sections.heading: What To Avoid
items: Deploying unbuilt generated artifacts.
Changing generated files directly on the server.
Using local sample data in production.
Sharing test infrastructure with production.
Disabling security to make deployment easier.
Making environment-specific changes in framework source.
Deploying with unclear active module ownership.
Mixing sample data with production initialization data.
